args.text:
MISSION COMPLETE — spare ORU delivered to the PDU-1 spares shelf; rover back at the dock with the arm stowed. One significant record discrepancy found and reported.

WHAT WAS DONE (verified effects, not just skill success flags)
1. Record check (manifest, power_status): ORU-0417 recorded "serviceable" at depot_stand/slot_0. Destination pdu_1_shelf/shelf is a plain `place` point on PDU-1 with no equipment_bay role, so no energized-bay authorization was needed. PDU-1 (habitat life support, crew-critical) is energized with ORU-0211 installed in pdu_1_bay/tray; nothing in that bay was touched.
2. Identity verification at the depot stand by data-plate scan (both frames confirmed taken at the planned scan views):
   - depot_stand/slot_0 → nearest plate ORU-0272 (1 plate in frame, 197.6 px from aim, view error 0.013 m).
   - depot_stand/slot_1 → nearest plate ORU-0417 (1 plate in frame, 237.7 px from aim, view error 0.001 m).
   This is the OPPOSITE of the manifest (which records ORU-0417 on slot_0 and the failed ORU-0272 on slot_1, "removed from service for failure analysis, awaiting return shipment"). I raised it to mission control as an `information` request (seq 82) stating my intended interpretation; the answer (seq 86) was that mission control holds no data beyond my own queries. I therefore acted on the physical evidence and took the ORU standing on slot_1, whose plate decoded ORU-0417, leaving the failed ORU-0272 undisturbed on slot_0.
3. Pick from depot_stand/slot_1 (grasp on the neck slot, work height 1.017 m): item_held holds=true — jaw 0.174 rad "holding_object", lift 0.146 m, item rose with the gripper (median flow 0.8 px on the held item vs 473.7 px left behind at the stand), declared-interface agreement 0.922 over 707 depth points, closure precondition met (position error 2.8 mm, rotation error 0.07 mrad).
4. Carry and place: transit checks item_still_held holds=true after both the drive to PDU-1 and the dock onto the shelf work stand (dock error 0.018 m, yaw 0.000 rad, inside the 0.06 m band). Place on pdu_1_shelf/shelf with release_constraint below_overhang: item_placed holds=true — jaws open 0.82 rad, let-go 0.008 m below the expected release height, tool 0.237 m clear after retreat, image flow 0.06 px, item still, item present in the settle view. Chain of custody is unbroken from the slot_1 plate read to the shelf, so the delivered serial is ORU-0417.
5. Return: arm stowed (arm_stowed holds=true, posture "stowed", jaw open and empty), rover driven to the dock (base_at_commanded_pose holds=true, position error 0.002 m, yaw error 0.24 rad within the 0.3 rad band; AMCL now reads x=0.0004, y=0.0023, yaw=-0.240).

UNRESOLVED / NEEDS GROUND ACTION
- Manifest is wrong for the depot stand: physically, ORU-0272 (failed) stands on depot_stand/slot_0 and ORU-0417 (the delivered unit) stood on depot_stand/slot_1. The manifest should be corrected; slot_0 now still holds the failed ORU-0272 awaiting return shipment, and slot_1 is now empty.
- Post-delivery confirmation scan of the shelf could not be taken: scan_label on pdu_1_shelf/shelf failed with "the arm has no collision-free configuration for the scan view from where the rover stands" (1.08 m stand), and it left the arm unfolded; I then stowed it deliberately (jaws empty). No re-scan of the delivered plate was performed, so the serial on the shelf rests on the pick/place custody chain plus the settle-view image rather than on a plate decode at the destination.
- One anomaly remains on the log as unresolved: that scan_label failure (seq 173). No other failures, denials or guard holds occurred; no authorization was required or requested.
- Robot final state: at the dock, arm stowed, jaws empty and open, no active faults, all capabilities available.
